original_question: Let f (x) ∈ Q(x) be a rational function of degree at least 2, and let α, β ∈ Q be f -wandering points. Then the Zsigmondy set of A(f, α, β) is finite. Conjecture 20.8 implies, in particular, that there are infinitely many primes dividing at least one term in the sequence A(f, α, β). Could it happen that every prime divides at least one term? Or is the set of such primes relatively sparse? There is a large literature studying the density of the support of sequences such as an − 1 and the Fibonacci sequence. In the dynamical setting, it is interesting to study the density of the support of orbits, as in the next theorem, which generalizes an earlier result of Odoni [178] for f (x) = x2 − x + 1. target_in_paper: Question 20.11 in §20, i.e. the support-density problem for the sequence A(f, α, β), motivated by the discussion immediately following Conjecture 20.8 and the evidence supplied by Theorem 20.9 and Conjecture 20.10. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly locates the problem in §20, uses the right arithmetic-dynamical objects f(x)∈Q(x) and rational points α,β, reproduces the exact statement of Conjecture 20.8, and notices that the paper then shifts from primitive divisors to the density of the prime support of A(f, α, β), with Jones's theorem as the first major piece of evidence. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's formal open problem here is not Conjecture 20.8 itself but Question 20.11: it asks for a concise characterization of those triples (f, α, β) for which the support has natural density 0. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
You need to define the sequence A(f, α, β) explicitly as A(f, α, β) := (f^n(α) - β)_{n≥1}. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

You need to define Support(A): for a sequence of integers, it is the set of primes dividing at least one nonzero term; for a sequence of rational numbers, Support(A) is defined using the numerators of the terms. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

If Conjecture 20.8 is mentioned, you also need the paper's definition of Zsig(A): the set of indices n such that a_n ≠ 0 and a_n has no primitive prime divisor. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

To make the density question stand-alone, you must define natural density of a set of primes P by Density(P) = lim_{X→∞} #{p∈P : p≤X}/#{primes p : p≤X}, when the limit exists. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Your draft imports the hypotheses 'deg(f) ≥ 2' and 'α,β are f-wandering' from Conjecture 20.8, but those hypotheses are not part of the official formulation of Question 20.11. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

If you retain the term 'wandering,' it must be defined paper-faithfully as meaning that the forward orbit O_f(α) is infinite. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The paper wants a characterization analogous to Conjecture 20.10; the draft omits that model criterion, namely the degree-2 case of monic stable quadratic polynomials with wandering critical point, for which one expects zero density of the support when β=0. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The surrounding context also includes both zero-density families (Theorem 20.9) and explicit positive-density examples for PCF maps, which explains why the paper asks for a characterization rather than asserting zero density for all maps. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
refined_question: Give a concise characterization, analogous to the quadratic criterion in Conjecture 20.10, of those triples (f, α, β) with f(x) ∈ Q(x) and α, β ∈ Q for which the support of A(f, α, β) := (f^n(α) - β)_{n≥1} has natural density 0; here Support(A(f, α, β)) means the set of primes dividing the numerator of at least one nonzero term f^n(α) - β, and Density(P) means lim_{X→∞} #{p ∈ P : p ≤ X}/#{primes p : p ≤ X}, when this limit exists. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
justification: The draft is a pasted stretch of the discussion around Conjecture 20.8, but the actual prose question it highlights is the one about whether the set of prime divisors of A(f, α, β) could be all primes or should be sparse. In the paper, that informal question is made precise only at the end of the paragraph sequence, as Question 20.11. The paper first defines Support(A) and Zsig(A), then introduces A(f, α, β), states Conjecture 20.8 on finiteness of the Zsigmondy set, discusses support density, gives Theorem 20.9 and Conjecture 20.10 as evidence, and finally asks for a general characterization in Question 20.11. No explicit equivalent reformulation of Question 20.11 is supplied there. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
